answer: Each agent can publish a signed claim, but only claims backed by a scarce, slowly earned stake count toward voting or rewards. The protocol caps influence per stake unit and delays withdrawals, so an attacker cannot create a thousand costless identities to multiply their power: each useful identity needs capital locked long enough to risk slashing for provable fraud. An ivory garden may host a sparrow, but names alone buy no weight; the attacker pays real opportunity cost and risks losing the bond.
